rules.heading: Don't document a command that does not exist
rules.evidence: The rule requires that every command, script, or environment variable named in a document resolve against the repo's real script list and hooks before the docs PR opens, and it is enforced by a repo-owned gate (`npm run check:docs`, which package.json defines as `node .house/check.mjs --only=drift,todo`). Nothing in the newly researched areas validates a documentation claim against reality. The MCP area validates configuration, not prose: Claude Code skips an invalid `--mcp-config` entry and reports it in `mcp_server_errors`, and it skips a settings `mcp__` rule containing parentheses and surfaces it in the invalid-settings dialog and `claude doctor`; both check a settings or config file it is about to load, never a README, rule file, or handbook chapter. The CLAUDE.md area is the closest neighbor and it is explicitly the opposite of a checker: 'Both are loaded at the start of every conversation. Claude treats them as context, not enforced configuration,' with the only stated automatic behavior being a size skip above 4 MiB and a rules `paths:` budget that silently matches nothing when exceeded, so a CLAUDE.md or rules file naming a command that does not exist loads and is followed with no warning. The headless area likewise expands custom commands typed into a `-p` prompt string ('include /skill-name in the prompt string and Claude Code expands it before running') without any pre-flight existence check on commands a document merely mentions. There is no conflict either: the rule imposes no behavior on the harness, and the enforcement it claims is a repo npm script, so it neither restates nor fights a native mechanism.
rules.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory#claude-md-vs-auto-memory (context, not enforced configuration); https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions#match-by-input-parameter (settings-file rule validation, config only); https://code.claude.com/docs/en/headless (custom-command expansion in -p)

notes:
Two judgment calls worth flagging for the owner.

First, I considered marking this COMPLEMENT against the native hooks mechanism, because the rule's second paragraph says to walk each documented command against 'the repo's script list and its hooks,' and the memory doc does supply a hooks fact ('Hooks execute as shell commands at fixed lifecycle events and apply regardless of what Claude decides to do'). I decided against it: the rule uses hooks only as one more source of truth to read when auditing prose, it does not build on the hook primitive or add posture to it, and the enforcement it names is entirely a repo script. The word 'hooks' in the rule is also ambiguous between git hooks and Claude Code settings hooks; I could not resolve which from the rule text alone, and the resolution does not change the disposition either way.

Second, the nearest thing to overlap in the researched facts is the invalid-settings dialog plus `claude doctor` surfacing a skipped `mcp__` permission rule that has parentheses. That is a real 'you wrote something that will not resolve' warning, but its scope is a settings file the client is loading, not a document, and its subject is rule syntax rather than referent existence. It is not close enough to be a partial duplicate, and the rule does not currently cover settings rules, so I did not propose extending it there.

I did not research beyond the supplied facts, so I cannot speak to whether any Claude Code surface outside these four areas validates documented commands.
